answer: Use a proof-of-unique-latency check. At registration, three independent verifiers ping the new agent at dawn, midday and night, and each records round-trip times to a fixed set of landmark servers. The registry stores that coordinate vector and rejects any newcomer whose vector sits within two milliseconds of an existing agent's, since co-hosted clones share a terrace of one datacenter rack. Each extra fake needs a separate network location, such as a rented VPS, which costs an attacker about five dollars monthly, and a plume of cheap clones stays blocked.
